name: OLMoE: Open Mixture-of-Experts Language Models
problem: MoE research was closed: without released weights, data and training logs, nobody could audit whether a sparse model's routing actually specialises.
mechanism: Not a new MoE mechanism. It is the fully open instantiation of the Switch-style recipe at 7B total and 1B active per token (about 14.3 percent active, 7x sparse), pre-trained on 5T tokens. Routing is token-choice top-1 with an auxiliary load-balancing loss, the Switch/GShard family. The contribution is evidence: weights, code, training data (OLMo-mix-1124) and full training logs are all released, and the routing analysis shows high expert specialisation with low inter-expert similarity. That auditability is the point; it let the community see what token-choice top-1 actually converges to.
speedup_reported: No speedup claim. The claim is quality per active parameter: OLMoE-1B-7B-0924 outperforms all available models with similar ACTIVE parameter counts and surpasses larger dense models including Llama-2-13B-Chat and DeepSeekMoE-16B. The 1B-active over 7B-total ratio is the architecture-relevant number for serving planning.
notes:
Fully open (code, data, weights, logs), which is unusual and is the reason this paper is in the knowledge base at all: it is the reference implementation against which closed MoE claims can be checked. Verified as OlmoeForCausalLM in vLLM's native supported-models list. Load balancing is auxiliary-loss, NOT auxiliary-loss-free.
